findings.finding: STEngine capture calls VEPerformanceManager.EvaluateVE, which assigns a new current bitrate.
findings.impact: A nominally passive health observation changes VisionEngine policy state.
findings.closure: NLTestSTEngineTests.STEngine_performance_observation_does_not_mutate_vision_bitrate_policy passed RED-GREEN; full suite 390/390 and Release build 0 warnings/errors.

findings.finding: STEngine imports concrete VECoreRuntime, LERuntimeManager and engine-specific snapshot types.
findings.impact: ST cannot be constructed or tested as a neutral observer without concrete engine implementations.
findings.closure: ST now imports only NOVORA.Contracts.Stability, classifies immutable neutral snapshots, and receives engine-specific adapters solely from the UI composition root. The architecture check found zero concrete VE/LE/ExIn imports under STEngine; NLTestSTEngineTests passed 9/9 and the full .NET suite passed 391/391.

findings.finding: ExInControlSession imports four internal VE areas while VEControlManager imports ExInEngine.
findings.impact: ExIn session ownership and VE control ownership are bidirectionally coupled.
findings.closure: ExInEngine and VisionEngine now share NOVORA.Contracts.Input only. VEControlManager implements the neutral contract; ExIn translates its internal device/action models at its boundary; the cross-engine physical coordinator moved to NOVORA.Integration. Both engine directories contain zero mutual imports, focused boundary/ExIn tests passed 73/73, Release build passed with 0 warnings/errors, and the full suite passed 392/392 against the real Windows cryptographic profile.

findings.finding: VisionEngine requires and deploys scrcpy-server 4.1 and starts its server class through app_process.
findings.impact: Runtime Dependency on scrcpy is nonzero; independence cannot yet be claimed.
findings.closure: G0 inventory/provenance and G1 explicit backend/dependency state pass. G2-G5 remain blocked by the absence of a NOVORA Android Agent candidate and physical parity evidence; Runtime Dependency remains nonzero and scrcpy cannot be retired. See NLDocumentationNovoraProtocolAndScrcpyGates.md.

findings.finding: Architecture rules describe five active LinkEngine sessions while current product specifications and manuals define one active phone per PC.
findings.impact: Session ownership and capacity tests have conflicting acceptance criteria.
findings.closure: ADR-009 selects one active cross-engine session and docs/ARCHITECTURE-RULES.md now agrees.

findings.finding: External process execution is distributed across service, engine, discovery, update and UI classes.
findings.impact: Path, argument, cancellation and cleanup policy cannot be audited through one contract today.
findings.closure: Every launcher category is classified in NLDocumentationProcessOwnership.md. NLServiceProcess now validates absolute paths/directories and structured arguments, captures output/error/exit code, and kills cancelled process trees. Finite VE Exchange and LE failover ADB adapters migrated; persistent protocol owners remain specialized. Negative/output/cancellation tests passed 3/3 and Release build passed with 0 warnings/errors.

findings.finding: The A/B baseline and ADR-001 through ADR-009 are present.
findings.impact: Implementation tasks now have approved ownership and migration decisions.
findings.closure: ADR pack is complete and internally consistent.

findings.finding: RelayCore tests pass but compile with 21 warnings and net2 is reported as future-incompatible.
findings.impact: Future Rust toolchains may reject a dependency and warning noise can conceal new defects.
findings.closure: The 21 project-owned unused-import and explicit-lifetime warnings were removed mechanically and the offline Release suite still passes 34/34 with 1 ignored benchmark. The finding remains CONFIRMED because mio 0.6 still brings net2 0.2.39, which Cargo reports as future-incompatible; upgrading the network stack requires a dedicated migration and runtime parity evidence.
